root_cause.text: The ARM32 SP804 delay-timer path incorrectly reused the sched_clock-backed `sp804_clkevt` instance, so `read_current_timer()` could dereference an uninitialized `sched_clkevt` when SP804 was not selected as `sched_clock`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit says that when `use_sched_clock` is not set, `sched_clkevt` is “not properly initialized,” yet `sp804_register_delay_timer()` was still called and `read_current_timer()` “calls sp804_read on an uninitialized sched_clkevt, leading to a kernel Oops”; the patch fixes this by introducing a dedicated `delay_clkevt` and changing `sp804_read_delay_timer_read()` to read `delay_clkevt->value` directly, while moving delay-timer registration after `clkevt = sp804_clkevt_get(base)`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The SP804 timer driver reused the same `sp804_clkevt` instance for both `sched_clock` and the ARM32 delay timer, so `sp804_register_delay_timer()` could publish a `read_current_timer()` callback that dereferenced an uninitialized `sched_clkevt` when SP804 was not selected as `sched_clock`.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch says `sp804_register_delay_timer` was called unconditionally even when `sp804_clocksource_and_sched_clock_init(..., use_sched_clock)` did not initialize `sched_clkevt`, and the diff fixes this by introducing a separate `delay_clkevt` pointer and changing `sp804_read_delay_timer_read()` to use `delay_clkevt->value` instead of `sp804_read()`/`sched_clkevt->value`.

root_cause_review.feedback: The root cause is mostly consistent with the CVE, but the supporting evidence is not fully accurate. The patch does not say `sp804_register_delay_timer` published a callback that dereferenced an uninitialized `sched_clkevt` via `sp804_read()` in the general case; it specifically moves delay timer registration to use a dedicated `delay_clkevt` and makes `sp804_read_delay_timer_read()` read `delay_clkevt->value` directly. Also, the claim that the same `sp804_clkevt` instance was reused for both `sched_clock` and the ARM32 delay timer is present in the description, but the evidence should explicitly note that the bug occurs because `delay_timer` used the sched_clock-backed instance before `sched_clkevt` was set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Bind the ARM delay timer to the correct hardware counter so delay reads use the registered timer instance instead of the global sched clock source.
intent_record.what: The delay timer registration function was changed to take a `struct sp804_clkevt *clk` argument instead of only an `int freq`, a new static `delay_clkevt` pointer was added under `CONFIG_ARM`, the delay timer read callback was changed from calling `sp804_read()` to directly reading `delay_clkevt->value`, and the `sp804_register_delay_timer()` implementation now stores the passed clockevent pointer before registering the delay timer. The non-ARM stub was updated to match the new function signature. A comment was also added above this block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the delay timer now reads from the specific hardware counter associated with the clockevent passed into registration, rather than relying on the global sched clockevent source. This binds the delay timer to the correct timer instance and prevents incorrect delay-timer reads when the sched clock source is not the right backing counter for delay timing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove delay timer registration from SP804 clocksource/sched clock initialization.
intent_record.what: The call to `sp804_register_delay_timer(rate);` was removed from `sp804_clocksource_and_sched_clock_init()`, leaving the subsequent `clkevt = sp804_clkevt_get(base);` call and timer control write unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the SP804 delay timer is no longer registered during this initialization path, so the delay timer setup now relies on some other code path or is intentionally omitted from this function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the SP804 clockevent as a delay timer during clocksource and sched clock initialization.
intent_record.what: A new call to sp804_register_delay_timer(clkevt, rate); was inserted after clocksource_mmio_init(...) and before the use_sched_clock conditional in sp804_clocksource_and_sched_clock_init().
intent_record.how: At runtime, the SP804 clockevent device is now also registered as a delay timer candidate using the current clockevent pointer and timer rate, enabling delay-loop timing support to be set up during initialization.

The root cause is the incorrect reuse of the SP804 sched_clock-backed clkevt instance in the delay-timer path. Removing delay timer registration from SP804 clocksource/sched clock initialization directly addresses that faulty reuse and prevents the invalid read_current_timer() path.

candidates.rationale: This registers the ARM delay timer during SP804 initialization, but it was incorrectly tied to the global sched_clock-backed SP804 instance, causing delay reads to reuse the wrong timer object and potentially dereference an uninitialized sched_clkevt when SP804 was not used as sched_clock.
This read path directly depends on sched_clkevt, so if the delay timer path reuses the sched_clock-backed instance improperly, this dereference becomes unsafe when sched_clkevt was never initialized.
The delay timer read function delegates to sp804_read(), which in turn uses sched_clkevt; that coupling is the core of the bug when the timer was not selected as sched_clock.
This registers the delay timer instance, so if the instance is wired to the wrong backing read function, the ARM delay timer subsystem will invoke the unsafe sched_clkevt-based read path.
